literal: Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, younger brother Shigui, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, Lu Qubing
idiomatic: Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, his younger brother Shigui, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, and Lu Qubing

literal: The former kings divided and ordered the realm, shepherded the black-haired people, used penal law to forbid their wickedness, and used ritual teaching to guard against their desires.
idiomatic: Former kings divided the realm and tended the people, using penal law to forbid wickedness and ritual teaching to guard against desire.

literal: Therefore offices were divided and officials appointed to govern the realm together.
idiomatic: Therefore they divided offices and appointed officials to govern the realm together.

literal: The Book says: "To know men is to be wise; to be able to place men in office and settle men is to be gracious.
idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "To know men is wisdom; to place men in office and settle the people is grace.

literal: " A wise and perspicacious lord is sure to obtain clear and bright ministers; a benighted and chaotic court has many greedy and cruel clerks.
idiomatic: " A wise ruler wins clear-minded ministers; a benighted court breeds greedy, cruel officials.

literal: Gao Huan set right the disorder and turned back to the proper, with pity for the hidden in his breast, so among prefects and magistrates many were fit for their posts.
idiomatic: Gao Huan set the realm right after chaos and held pity close, so many prefects and magistrates proved fit for their posts.

literal: Yet he still sent generals of battle merit out to pasture the outer marches; they did not know the substance of governance and had not heard of the arts of rule.
idiomatic: Yet he still sent battle-hardened generals to govern the outer marches—men who knew nothing of governance and had never learned the arts of rule.

literal: Not only were they dark to words and deeds of old, they even began by learning to hand cases to clerks by precedent; insatiable in exaction, unceasing in debauchery and cruelty—though sometimes the straight cord was applied, in the end there was no repentance or reform.
idiomatic: They were blind not only to precedent but even began by learning to hand cases to clerks by template; insatiable in levies, relentless in cruelty—though the law was sometimes enforced, they never truly reformed.

literal: Alas!
idiomatic: Alas!

literal: This was a great loss of the court.
idiomatic: This was a grave loss for the court.

literal: After Daining, elegance and refinement were both lacking; offices and prisons were sold, above and below deceived one another, and down to the final years venal goods grew still worse.
idiomatic: After the Daining era, refinement vanished; offices and judgments were sold, court and country deceived one another, and in the dynasty's last years venality grew worse still.

literal: Among Qi there were good officials such as Xin Shu—not one alone—many of whom rose to prominence through rank and title and have separate biographies.
idiomatic: Northern Qi had good officials—Xin Shu was not alone—many of whom won rank and fame and have their own biographies.

literal: Men such as Fang Zhonggan, able at the end of Wuping to stand out from the crowd, are all the more worthy of praise.
idiomatic: Men such as Fang Zhonggan, who at the end of Wuping still stood apart from the crowd, are all the more praiseworthy.

literal: Now Zhang Huayuan and the rest are gathered and listed in Good Officials.
idiomatic: Here Zhang Huayuan and the rest are gathered under Good Officials.

literal: Zhang Huayuan, style Guoman, was a man of Dai commandery.
idiomatic: Zhang Huayuan, style Guoman, was from Dai commandery.

literal: In youth he was bright and keen, with capacity and measure.
idiomatic: As a youth he was bright and keen, with real capacity.

literal: When Gao Huan opened the Rapid Cavalry Office he brought him in as legal-cases staff officer, promoted him to staff of the Grand Chancellor's office, and still attended at his side.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan opened the Rapid Cavalry Office he made Huayuan a legal-cases staff officer, then a staff member of the Grand Chancellor's office, still attending at his side.

literal: He followed him to Xindu and was deeply favored and treated by Gao Huan.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan to Xindu and was deeply favored.

literal: Whenever Gao Huan issued orders to the three armies he often had Huayuan proclaim and explain his intent.
idiomatic: Whenever Gao Huan commanded the three armies he often had Huayuan proclaim his intent.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first held Yong province, Gao Huan still wished to enlighten him with right and wrong and sent Huayuan into the passes to persuade him.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first held Yong province, Gao Huan still hoped to persuade him with the logic of loyalty and rebellion and sent Huayuan through the passes to argue with him.

literal: Zhou Wen secretly intended detention and said to Huayuan: "If you can bend your swift horse's legs here, we shall share wealth and honor together; if not, your life hangs on this day.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen secretly meant to detain him and said: "If you can bend your swift horse's legs to stay here, we shall share wealth and honor; if not, your life ends today.

literal: " Huayuan said: "The Prince of Bohai was born to order the age—perhaps Heaven set him free. With your lordship's petty hold on the western passes you have cut yourselves off, so Huayuan was sent to carry your lordship's message.
idiomatic: " Huayuan said: "The Prince of Bohai was born to order the age—perhaps Heaven itself set him free. Your lordship holds only the western passes and has cut yourselves off; Huayuan was sent to carry your message.

literal: If your lordship will not on this day change your plan and turn calamity into blessing, yet wish to bestow coercion, there is only death.
idiomatic: If you will not change course today and turn calamity into blessing, but mean to coerce me, there is only death.

literal: " Zhou Wen admired his candor and uprightness and sent him back east.
idiomatic: " Zhou Wen admired his candor and sent him back east.

literal: Gao Huan, because Huayuan had long not returned, often sighed in regret; when he heard he had come, joy showed in his face.
idiomatic: Gao Huan had long sighed over Huayuan's absence; when he heard of his return, joy showed on his face.

literal: Through successive promotions he became inspector of Yan province; the people were moved and attached themselves, and bandits and robbers lay quiet.
idiomatic: Promoted in time to inspector of Yan, he won the people's attachment and banditry ceased.

literal: The provincial prison had formerly held more than a thousand prisoners; Huayuan decided and released them all.
idiomatic: The provincial prison had held more than a thousand prisoners; Huayuan judged and released them all.

literal: At year's end only several dozen men of heavy crime remained; Huayuan also sent them home to offer New Year's congratulations, to return to prison on schedule.
idiomatic: At year's end only several dozen men of serious crime remained; Huayuan sent even them home for New Year's greetings, on promise to return to prison on schedule.

literal: Before this, within the province fierce beasts had often ravaged; from the time Huayuan took the province, suddenly six piebald horses devoured them— all took it as the effect of transforming influence.
idiomatic: Before, fierce beasts had often ravaged the province; once Huayuan took office, six piebald horses suddenly devoured them—all called it the fruit of his transforming influence.

literal: Later he died in office; great and small among the people all cried out in longing.
idiomatic: He later died in office; people great and small mourned him aloud.

literal: Song Shiliang, style Yuanyou, was a man of Guangping.
idiomatic: Song Shiliang, style Yuanyou, was from Guangping.

literal: At fifteen he already had daring spirit; he answered the call and followed the army on the northern campaign, repeatedly winning battle merit.
idiomatic: At fifteen he already had daring; he enlisted for the northern campaign and won battle merit again and again.

literal: Soon he became attendant censor of the palace and went to Hebei to register households, greatly uncovering hidden and idle persons.
idiomatic: Soon he became palace attendant censor and went to Hebei to register households, uncovering many hidden and idle persons.

literal: On his return he saw many bones beside Jiyin city and sent letters to the provinces and commanderies ordering all collected and buried.
idiomatic: Returning, he saw many bones beside Jiyin city and wrote the provinces and commanderies to collect and bury them all.

literal: That night sweet rain poured in torrents.
idiomatic: That night sweet rain poured down.

literal: On his return, Emperor Xiaozhuang rewarded him, saying: "I know the households you registered doubled the original rolls; if every official were so intent, it would be like bringing forth another realm under Heaven."
idiomatic: Back at court, Emperor Xiaozhuang praised him: "The households you registered doubled the original rolls; if every official worked like you, it would be as if another realm had appeared under Heaven."

literal: He went out and was removed to be prefect of Qinghe.
idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Qinghe.

literal: Shiliang's talent and insight were clear and bright, especially skilled in the arts of rule; within the commandery, before long, his reputation was very high.
idiomatic: Shiliang was clear and bright in talent, especially skilled in governance; within the commandery his fame rose quickly.

literal: Southeast of the commandery was the Crooked Dike, where the Cheng clan alone blocked and dwelt and many bandits gathered.
idiomatic: Southeast of the commandery lay Crooked Dike, where the Cheng clan alone held the ground and bandits gathered thickly.

literal: Men made a saying of it: "Better cross the Wu region and Kuaiji than pass Cheng's Crooked Dike.
idiomatic: People said: "Better cross Wu and Kuaiji than pass Cheng's Crooked Dike.

literal: " Shiliang applied the eight-article system and the bandits fled to other districts.
idiomatic: " Shiliang applied his eight-article system and the bandits fled to other districts.

literal: The people again made a rhyme: "Though Crooked Dike is steep, what good are the bandits?—so long as Lord Song screens their tracks.
idiomatic: The people rhymed: "Though Crooked Dike is steep, what good are bandits?—Lord Song alone screens their tracks.

literal: " Later in the Tianbao era's great amnesty, the commandery had not a single prisoner beforehand; the clerks merely bowed to the edict.
idiomatic: " Later, at Tianbao's great amnesty, the commandery had not one prisoner beforehand—the clerks only bowed to the edict.

literal: Inside the prison millet grew, and peach trees and artemisia filled it too.
idiomatic: Inside the prison millet grew, and peach trees and artemisia filled the yards.

literal: Daily the yamen gate stood empty and still, with no more litigants.
idiomatic: Daily the yamen gate stood empty; no one came to sue.

literal: That winter, sweet springs appeared within the borders.
idiomatic: That winter sweet springs appeared within the borders.

literal: When he was replaced and left, the whole city saw him off on the road.
idiomatic: When he was replaced, the whole city saw him off.

literal: An old man, Ding Jingang, wept and came forward, saying: "I am ninety and recall thirty-five administrations; my lord is not only skilled in rule—your clarity goes clean through.
idiomatic: An old man, Ding Jingang, wept and came forward: "I am ninety and recall thirty-five administrations; you govern well, and your clarity goes clean through.

literal: Now we lose a worthy lord—how shall the people be saved?
idiomatic: Now we lose a worthy magistrate—how shall the people be saved?

literal: " None failed to cling and weep.
idiomatic: " None failed to cling to him in tears.

literal: He was appointed prefect of Dong commandery and died in office.
idiomatic: He was made prefect of Dong commandery and died in office.

literal: Shiliang studied hard and loved composing text; he wrote Outline of Characters in five chapters and Song Clan Separate Records in ten scrolls.
idiomatic: Shiliang studied hard and loved writing; he composed Outline of Characters in five chapters and Song Clan Separate Records in ten scrolls.

literal: He and his younger brother Shigui both had a reputation for filial piety and brotherly affection.
idiomatic: He and his younger brother Shigui both won fame for filial piety and brotherly affection.

literal: Shigui, from youth stern and orderly, loved the law; he was gradually promoted to minister of justice.
idiomatic: Shigui, stern from youth, loved the law and rose in time to minister of justice.

literal: The people of Luo province gathered intending to seize the Yellow River bridge; officials arrested and tried them, implicating more than seventeen hundred men of the Yuan clique and their associates.
idiomatic: People of Luo province gathered to seize the Yellow River bridge; officials arrested them and implicated more than seventeen hundred Yuan clansmen and associates.

literal: Cui Xuan was minister of justice and took it for rebellion; for years the case was not closed.
idiomatic: Cui Xuan as minister of justice called it rebellion; for years the case would not close.

literal: When Shigui became vice minister, he judged the matter to be robbery.
idiomatic: When Shigui became vice minister, he judged the matter robbery.

literal: Thereupon the ringleaders were executed and the rest who followed in guilt were all released.
idiomatic: The ringleaders were executed; the rest were all released.

literal: At the time the chief justice of the Court Su Zhenzhi was also known for balanced competence.
idiomatic: At the time Court chief justice Su Zhenzhi was also known for balanced competence.

literal: Within the ministry they made a saying: "To decide doubtful guilt, Su Zhenzhi; to see the inside from the table, Song Shigui.
idiomatic: In the ministry they said: "To decide doubtful guilt—Su Zhenzhi; to see inside from the table—Song Shigui.

literal: " Men of the time took them as the ministry's twin marvels.
idiomatic: " Men of the time called them the ministry's twin marvels.

literal: Prisoners from the Southern Terrace arriving at the Court of Justice—Shigui often cleared them.
idiomatic: Prisoners sent from the Southern Terrace to the Court of Justice—Shigui often cleared them.

literal: He was then transferred to investigating censor and was about to inquire into their abuses; the commandant Bi Yiyun would not deliver them, and though the transfer went back and forth it did not stop.
idiomatic: Transferred to investigating censor, he meant to inquire into their abuses; commandant Bi Yiyun would not hand prisoners over, and the exchanges would not end.

literal: Shigui then submitted a memorial, speaking to the utmost of Yiyun's cruel overreach.
idiomatic: Shigui memorialized, denouncing Yiyun's cruel overreach to the full.

literal: Emperor Xianzong summoned the two men and in person charged Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long deceived the Court; you can hold to principle and contend with them—only keep this heart and do not worry that you will not be rich and honored.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong summoned both and told Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long deceived the Court; hold to principle against them—keep this heart and you need not fear missing wealth and honor.

literal: " He charged Yiyun: "What you have done of late truly deserves death; because your aim is to hate evil, for now you are pardoned once.
idiomatic: " He told Yiyun: "Your recent conduct truly deserves death; because you aim to hate evil, you are pardoned once.

literal: " He then turned to the court and said: "These two are both my bone-in-the-throat ministers.
idiomatic: " He turned to the court: "These two are both ministers who stick in my throat.

literal: " When he died of illness, the imprisoned of the Court of Justice and the censorate, hearing Shigui was dead, all wept: "Minister Song of the Court is dead—where is our road to life!"
idiomatic: " When he died, prisoners of the Court and censorate wept: "Court Minister Song is dead—where is our road to life?"

literal: Shiliang's nephew Xiaowang was learned and also loved gathering and stitching literary ornament.
idiomatic: Shiliang's nephew Xiaowang was learned and loved literary ornament.

literal: His form was short and ugly, yet he loved to praise and blame men; opinion of the time greatly detested this.
idiomatic: Short and ugly in form, he loved to praise and blame others; opinion of the time detested him.

literal: He became staff officer to Duan Xiaoyan's opening office and was again recommended as literary officer to the Prince of Beiping.
idiomatic: He became staff officer in Duan Xiaoyan's opening office and was recommended as literary officer to the Prince of Beiping.

literal: He sought entry into the Forest of Literature Hall and did not succeed; he therefore slandered court gentlemen and compiled Separate Records in twenty scrolls; when Qi was pacified he changed it to Eastern Pass Customs and Traditions, broadened what he had seen and heard, and presented more than thirty scrolls.
idiomatic: Denied the Forest of Literature Hall, he slandered court gentlemen and compiled Separate Records in twenty scrolls; when Qi fell he retitled it Eastern Pass Customs and Traditions, broadened his material, and presented more than thirty scrolls.

literal: His words were mostly wild error; the sections were redundant and confused, without the form of real authorship.
idiomatic: His words were mostly wild error; sections were redundant and confused, without real authorship.

literal: Lang Ji, style Shiye, was a man of Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Lang Ji, style Shiye, was from Zhongshan.

literal: His body was eight chi tall, with a fine beard; he ranged widely through the classics, especially skilled in clerkly affairs.
idiomatic: Eight chi tall, with a fine beard, he ranged through the classics and excelled at administrative affairs.

literal: He began his career as a court gentleman and was repeatedly promoted to defender of Haixi.
idiomatic: He began as a court gentleman and rose to defender of Haixi.

literal: Liang's Wu Mingche led troops to besiege Haixi; Ji encouraged soldiers and people and firmly defended for more than a hundred days; army grain was nearly gone and weapons exhausted, until they even carved wood for arrows and cut paper for fletching.
idiomatic: Wu Mingche of Liang besieged Haixi; Ji encouraged soldiers and people and held firm for more than a hundred days until grain and arms were gone—they carved wood for arrows and cut paper for fletching.

literal: When the siege lifted and he returned to court, Vice Director Yang Yin met and comforted him, saying: "You were a civil clerk, yet had military strategy.
idiomatic: When the siege lifted he returned; Vice Director Yang Yin met him: "You were a civil clerk, yet showed military strategy.

literal: Carving wood and cutting paper—there is no precedent for that; how could the thought of Ban and Mo be surpassed?"
idiomatic: Carving wood and cutting paper has no precedent—how could Ban and Mo's inventiveness be surpassed?"

literal: Later he held Yingchuan commandery concurrently; for years cases had stagnated, yet within days he judged and exhausted them all, and when the Terrace's reports came down they all accorded with what Ji had stated.
idiomatic: Later he held Yingchuan concurrently; cases had stagnated for years, yet within days he cleared them all, and Terrace reports approved what Ji had ruled.

literal: The statutes were already sparse, litigation quiet, and officials and people far and near all rejoiced together.
idiomatic: Statutes grew sparse, litigation quiet, and officials and people far and near rejoiced.

literal: Ji's nature was pure and cautious, with nothing he sought for himself; he once told others: "Where one serves in office, one need not even make a wooden pillow—how much less anything heavier than that.
idiomatic: Pure and cautious, he sought nothing for himself; he once said: "In office one need not even make a wooden pillow—how much less anything beyond that.

literal: " He only rather ordered books copied.
idiomatic: " He only had books copied.

literal: Pan Ziyi once sent him a letter saying: "To copy books in office is also a frivolous fault of fashion.
idiomatic: Pan Ziyi wrote: "Copying books in office is also a fashionable fault.

literal: " Ji answered: "To see fault and know benevolence—that too will do.
idiomatic: " Ji replied: "To see fault and know benevolence—that will do.

literal: " Later he died in office; when the coffin was to return, those far and near who escorted him none failed to cling to the carriage rails and weep.
idiomatic: " He later died in office; when the coffin was to return, escorts far and near clung to the carriage rails in tears.

literal: Meng Ye, style Jingye, was a man of Anguo in Julu.
idiomatic: Meng Ye, style Jingye, was from Anguo in Julu.

literal: His family was originally poor and low; in youth he was a provincial clerk.
idiomatic: His family was poor; in youth he was a provincial clerk.

literal: His nature was honest and cautious; colleagues who stole official silk divided thirty bolts for him and he refused and would not receive them.
idiomatic: Honest and cautious, when colleagues who stole official silk offered him thirty bolts he refused.

literal: Wei Prince of Pengcheng Shao was appointed to Ding province and made Ye records-and-keeper.
idiomatic: When Wei Prince of Pengcheng Shao took Ding province, Ye was made records-and-keeper.

literal: Chief Administrator Liu Renzhi said to Ye: "I stand outside, you dwell within; with one heart and shared strength, perhaps there can be success.
idiomatic: Chief Administrator Liu Renzhi told Ye: "I stand outside, you within; with one heart we may succeed.

literal: " Before long Renzhi was summoned in as director of the Secretariat; on the road he told Shao: "Among those around Your Highness whom you can trust there is only Meng Ye—wish to put sole trust in him.
idiomatic: " Soon Renzhi was summoned to the Secretariat; leaving, he told Shao: "Of those around you, only Meng Ye can be trusted—put sole trust in him.

literal: The rest cannot be trusted.
idiomatic: The rest cannot be trusted.

literal: " He also parted from Ye, took his hand, and said: "Now I leave the capital and you lose support; I fear that afterward you cannot preserve yourself.
idiomatic: " Parting from Ye he took his hand: "I leave the capital and you lose support; I fear you cannot preserve yourself afterward.

literal: Only uprightness and straightness—wish you to urge yourself.
idiomatic: Only uprightness and straightness—urge yourself.

literal: " Ye had only one horse; it died from thinness.
idiomatic: " Ye had only one horse; it died from thinness.

literal: Shao, because Ye's family was poor, ordered the provincial and commandery officials to eat the horse's flesh together, wishing to give generous compensation; Ye firmly declined and dared not accept.
idiomatic: Because Ye's family was poor, Shao ordered officials to eat the horse's flesh and meant to compensate him generously; Ye firmly declined.

literal: Shao then jested to Ye: "You invite a famous man's reputation.
idiomatic: Shao jested: "You court a famous man's reputation.

literal: " He answered: "Ye is minute and low, serving Your Highness in attendance; since I cannot benefit you, how could I damage your clear wind?
idiomatic: " Ye answered: "I am minute and low, serving in attendance; since I cannot benefit you, how could I damage your clear reputation?

literal: " Later Gao Huan wrote to Shao: "The records-keeper surnamed Meng is extremely able in intent—why not place him before your eyes.
idiomatic: " Later Gao Huan wrote Shao: "The records-keeper surnamed Meng is extremely attentive—why not keep him before your eyes?
